posts.headline: The line, alone on a dark ground
posts.caption:
Rest is the greatest gift.

We are a small studio in Melbourne making one very good sleep box, and a few silk masks. Follow along. We open this month.

posts.headline: Silk, close enough to see the weave
posts.shoot: Pillowcase folded in thirds, raking side light, cream ground. Sell the material before the product.
posts.caption:
Grade 6A mulberry silk at 22 momme. Heavy enough to drape properly, and heavy enough to survive being washed for years.

Everything in the box had to feel like this against a warm cheek at 2am.

posts.headline: Hands smoothing a pillowcase

posts.caption: The last thing you do before the light goes off.

Swipe for everything inside.

Mulberry silk eye mask. Silk pillowcase. Matching silk scrunchie. Bed socks. Pillow mist. Herbal tea. A small candle. A journal for the bedside table.

weeks.note: Changed from the original plan. The masks now exist and they are the cheapest way in, so they get a week rather than a mention.

posts.headline: The silk mask, flat, side lit
posts.shoot: Show the covered strap and the outside seam. Those are the two things nobody else does and both photograph.
posts.caption:
The seam sits on the outside, so nothing rests against your eyelid. The strap is covered along its whole length, so it does not catch in hair.

Small things. They are the whole reason this one took a year.

posts.headline: Four masks, four reasons
posts.shoot: One mask per slide, each on its own ground. Silk, weighted, contoured, travel.
posts.caption:
Four masks now. Silk for most people. Weighted at 180 grams if you like the feel of something there. Contoured if you want to open your eyes underneath it. Travel if it lives in a bag.

From $49, link in bio.

posts.headline: Cutting and finishing a strap
posts.shoot: The bench, close, hands only. Slight speed up is fine here.
posts.caption: Every strap is covered by hand. It is the slowest part of making a mask and the first thing you would notice if we skipped it.

posts.headline: Give the most important thing
posts.caption:
Give the most important thing.

The box is $149. The silk mask on its own is $49. Both leave Melbourne the same afternoon if you order before the cut-off.

posts.caption:
Two of us, one bench, about forty boxes on a good weekday.

Everything goes in the same order every time: tissue, pillowcase, mask, scrunchie, socks, then the four smaller pieces along the front so nothing moves in transit. The card goes in last, on top.

Your message, in pen, on a printed card, before the lid goes on.

Up to 250 characters and we write it exactly as you type it, line breaks and all. We will quietly fix an obvious typo in a name and leave the rest alone.

Silk, weighted, contoured, travel. Different jobs, same covered strap, because that is the part everyone else gets wrong.

From $49, link in bio.

tile.text: The last thing before the light goes off

posts.caption:
Two sprays on the pillow. Socks on. Phone in the other room, on a charger, with an actual alarm clock doing the waking.

What it is matters far less than that it never changes.

No pricing on the outside of the parcel either, so it can go straight to them.

Put their address at checkout and your words on the card. That is the whole thing.

Most silk in gift sets is 16 momme, and it is silk on the front with polyester behind.

Ours is 22 momme on both faces, cut from one run so the mask, the pillowcase and the scrunchie match exactly. It is the difference you feel in a year, not on day one.
